name: Maya marimba (Guatemalan Highland)
lineage: Maya marimba tradition of the Guatemalan Highlands (Quetzaltenango, Sololá, Huehuetenango departments) and adjacent Chiapas (Mexico), featuring large wooden-resonator marimba ensembles played by three-to-four marimberos simultaneously on a single instrument (marimba doble or marimba grande). The instrument arrived in the New World through West-African enslaved-population introduction and was adopted by the Maya highland communities as a distinctly Guatemalan-cultural-marker. Repertoire spans the canonical son chapín nineteenth-and-twentieth-century Guatemalan national-popular forms, religious-procession music for the cofradía saint-society celebrations, and contemporary popular and dance-band material. The Marimba de Concierto formal-conservatory tradition operates parallel to the village-marimba folk-tradition.
